subject: Deployment boundaries discussion — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@terrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment boundaries discussion — recap & next steps

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our side and suggested next steps so we have alignment heading into procurement.

Key pain points you highlighted:
- Data must remain in a US-resident environment (primary requirement: US-East).
- No outbound internet egress from the inference cluster; all updates must be pulled through a controlled pipeline.
- Regulatory driver: HIPAA + internal PCI-aligned controls for cardholder-adjacent data flows.
- Need customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and audit-level access logs for tokenization/requests.
- Low latency requirement between app layer and model inference (sub-80ms tail desired for 512-token flows).

Goals you articulated:
- Pilot with a subset of traffic by late-Jan 2027.
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem air-gapped) with dedicated GPU capacity.
- Clear handoff to procurement with an SOW + network checklist that maps to TerraHealth network ops controls.

Constraints we noted on the call:
- Egress: you asked that the inference nodes have no public internet egress. That implies either a fully air-gapped on-prem package or VPC with strict NAT/router controls and approved outbound proxy.
- Ports/protocols: expected list — HTTPS to a controlled updater, NTP via internal time service, and internal-only TLS to upstream app services.
- KMS: in-call ask — integration with your CloudHSM or on-prem HSM via key wrapping is required.

Attached: a focused "redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf" that we use to map network controls and firewall rules during discovery. Please review and flag anything missing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep dive with TerraHealth infra + security — include your Cloud/Network lead and HSM admin. Suggested window: next Tue/Wed (Oct 26/27) morning PT.
2) We'll provide a preliminary SOW ballpark and a template for terms (security annex, data residency clauses) within 3 business days after the deep dive.
3) Redwood solutions engineer will prepare a runbook for a staging canary test (non-prod, limited traffic).

Can you confirm attendees for the tech-deep-dive and whether Oct 26 morning PT works? Also, are there any additional attachment formats you want (CSV of allowed CIDR ranges, existing firewall rules)?

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@terrahealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: TerraHealth Security Team <security@terrahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment boundaries discussion — recap & next steps

Dylan — thanks for the clear notes and checklist. Quick clarifications and a couple of asks from our side:

1) Timeline: procurement is targeting Nov 30 for contract signature, so your Jan pilot timeline fits but we'll need a firm SOW in November to get budget approval.
2) HSM: yes — we own an AWS CloudHSM cluster but can also provide an on-prem HSM if needed. Important: the HSM admin (cc'ed on the security alias) needs details on key wrapping and whether Redwood will ever hold plaintext keys. Our policy: keys must be under TerraHealth control; no persistent plaintext export by vendor.
3) Egress: we prefer no public egress from the inference subnet. Updates to model weights or runtime images must be delivered via a controlled pull through a bastion/proxy that we manage.
4) Network columns: attaching our network ops matrix (terra-network-ops-matrix.xlsx) — it has the required CIDR ranges, permitted ports, and an existing list of allowed third-party endpoints (none preferred).

Confirming attendees for the tech-deep-dive: me, our Head of Infra (Priya Shah), and our HSM admin (Ajit Kumar). Oct 26, 09:00 PT works.

Also: please include an outline of any on-prem packaging differences (air-gapped installer vs VPC subscription model) in the SOW preview. We'll want a high-level runbook showing how you perform upgrades with zero egress.

-Sanjay
CTO, TerraHealth
(sanjay@terrahealth.com)

Attachment: terra-network-ops-matrix.xlsx

Thanks Dylan — I'm on for Oct 26, 09:00 PT. Initial notes below (will formalize slides/runbook by Oct 24):

HSM/KMS: we support BYOK models. Redwood never stores unwrapped customer master keys. For CloudHSM we support envelope encryption (customers keep CMKs in their HSM, we hold wrapped keys for runtime in a sealed vault). For on-prem HSMs we can support a connector pattern; engineering will need details on vendor (Thales/Cavium/etc.).

Egress & upgrades: we have two approaches:
- VPC private: Keep inference nodes in a private subnet with a restricted outbound proxy controlled by the customer. We push updates via a signed artifact registry pull initiated from a management host in your network.
- Air-gapped on-prem installer: full offline install using signed packages delivered by customer; we run validation micro-services in a sealed environment.
Both support the 'no public egress' requirement.

Networking: targeting sub-80ms tail requires colocating the GPU cluster in the same AZ as app infra; recommend 1–2 Gbps interconnect and MTU 9000 if your switch fabric supports it. We'll include a sample firewall/CIDR mapping in the runbook.

I'll pull an engineer (Miguel Santos) into the deep dive for the HSM/KMS and deployment packaging conversation.
